title: Support macros & snippets refresh (Escalation playbook + Known-issues sprint)
content:
Purpose
- Refresh Support macro library to be consistent across Hosted / Dedicated / Private.
- Make escalation asks copy/paste-ready (request IDs, regions, model, time window, customer tier).
- Ensure log collection instructions are customer-safe (no secrets, no full payloads, no internal links).
- Align wording with the refreshed escalation playbook + SLA policy.

Scope
- Macros for: intake, diagnostics, known-issues guidance, escalation requests, update cadence, “waiting on customer”, resolution follow-up.
- Macros should link to the Known Issues index where applicable.

Non-goals
- Replacing the Confluence playbook.
- Sharing customer-specific details or internal incident thresholds.

How to use (Support team)
- Choose the macro that matches the symptom first (streaming / 429 / dedicated scaling / private upgrade / audit logs).
- Always fill in placeholders before sending.
- If you link a known-issues article, also paste the 2–3 bullet “workaround steps” directly in the reply (customers should not have to hunt).
- For escalation pages, use the Escalation Ask template (Macro E-1) so on-call gets consistent context.

Placeholders (use exactly)
- {customer_name}
- {workspace_or_org_id}
- {ticket_key}
- {tier} (self_serve | dedicated | private | enterprise)
- {region}
- {endpoint} (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/embeddings, etc.)
- {model}
- {sdk} (python|ts|go|none)
- {sdk_version}
- {request_ids} (comma-separated)
- {time_window_utc} (e.g., 2026-02-18 16:20–16:45 UTC)
- {impact_summary} (1–2 lines)
- {next_update_time} (UTC)

Tone rules (keep consistent)
- Be direct, specific, and action-oriented.
- Don’t promise ETAs unless Engineering/SRE has provided one.
- Don’t disclose internal-only dashboards, internal incident numbers, or capacity details.

------------------------------------------------------------
A) Intake + required context

Macro A-1: “Thanks—request basics (copy/paste)”
Subject: Re: {short_issue_title}
Hi {customer_name} — thanks for the details. To help us triage quickly, can you confirm:
1) Deployment/tier: {tier}
2) Region: {region}
3) Endpoint + model: {endpoint} + {model}
4) SDK + version (or raw HTTP): {sdk} {sdk_version}
5) Approx time window (UTC): {time_window_utc}
6) Request IDs (x-request-id / request_id) for 3–5 failed requests: {request_ids}

If you don’t have request IDs, a timestamp window + approximate volume is still helpful.

Macro A-2: “How to find request IDs (customer-safe)”
Request IDs usually come back in the response headers (often `x-request-id`) and sometimes in the SDK response metadata.
- If you’re using our SDK: enable debug logging around the request and capture the request ID only (avoid logging full prompts or responses).
- If you’re using raw HTTP: log response headers for failed requests.

If you share logs, please redact:
- API keys / auth tokens
- Any end-user PII
- Full prompts/responses (high-level summaries are OK)

Macro A-3: “Customer-safe log bundle ask (general)”
If possible, please share a small diagnostic bundle with:
- 2–3 representative request IDs
- timestamps (UTC)
- region + model
- client runtime details (language, SDK version)
- error message + HTTP status code

Please do NOT include secrets (API keys, cookies, bearer tokens) or full user content.

------------------------------------------------------------
B) Status + SLA-aligned updates

Macro B-1: “Initial acknowledgement (SLA-safe)”
Hi {customer_name} — thanks for flagging this. We’re investigating now.

What we’re looking at:
- {impact_summary}

Next steps:
- We’ll review request traces for {request_ids} and check for any regional or model-specific degradation.

Next update:
- We’ll follow up by {next_update_time} (UTC), or sooner if we identify a mitigation/workaround.

Macro B-2: “Update (no new info yet)”
Hi {customer_name} — quick update: we’re still actively investigating and haven’t identified a definitive root cause yet.

What we’ve done so far:
- Reviewed request traces for {request_ids}
- Checked for correlated errors in {region}

What’s next:
- We’re continuing to isolate whether this is client/network behavior vs service-side.

Next update:
- By {next_update_time} (UTC)

Macro B-3: “Waiting on customer (keep SLA clear)”
Hi {customer_name} — we’re currently blocked on a couple details needed to proceed:
- {list_missing_items}

Once we have those, we’ll continue investigation immediately. If it’s easier, you can send:
- a timestamp window (UTC)
- 3–5 request IDs
- region + model

------------------------------------------------------------
C) Escalation asks (internal-facing to Eng/SRE via page/Slack bridge)

Macro E-1: “Escalation ask (paste into page/Slack bridge)”
Customer escalation summary
- Ticket: {ticket_key}
- Customer / org: {customer_name} / {workspace_or_org_id}
- Tier: {tier}
- Region: {region}
- Endpoint/model: {endpoint} / {model}
- Time window (UTC): {time_window_utc}
- Request IDs: {request_ids}
- Impact: {impact_summary}
- Current customer workaround attempts: {what_customer_tried}
- Severity suggestion (Support P0–P4): {p_level}
- Requested help:
  1) Confirm if service-side issue / known incident
  2) Any immediate mitigations we can suggest
  3) Owner + next update time

Links
- Slack bridge: {slack_channel_link}
- Related known-issue (if any): {kb_link}

Macro E-2: “When to pull SRE vs Platform (internal note)”
- Pull SRE when there is suspected regional degradation, elevated error rate, latency spikes, streaming health issues, or active incident coordination.
- Pull Platform for auth/SSO issues, quota/rate-limit enforcement anomalies, audit log pipeline issues, console/control-plane workflow problems.
- Pull Private Deployments/Platform for installer upgrades, migrations, cluster health, VPC DNS/networking.
(See Confluence escalation directory for exact contacts.)

------------------------------------------------------------
D) Known-issues responses (customer-facing)

Macro K-0: “Known-issues index link (short)”
We maintain a curated list of known issues + workarounds here: {known_issues_index_link}

If you can share your region/model and a couple request IDs, we can confirm whether your case matches a known issue.

Macro K-1: “Streaming timeouts / reconnect guidance (Hosted/Dedicated)”
Symptoms you described can happen when a streaming connection is interrupted mid-generation (e.g., proxy idle timeouts, client disconnects).

Recommended steps (safe defaults):
1) Set an explicit client-side read timeout appropriate for your max generation time.
2) Implement retry with backoff for transient disconnects; treat retries as new requests unless you have idempotency controls.
3) Ensure your network path (load balancer/proxy) supports long-lived connections for SSE/streaming.

If you share 3–5 request IDs + a timestamp window, we can confirm whether the disconnect occurred upstream or client-side.

Escalate to us immediately if:
- it impacts production traffic broadly
- it’s repeatable across multiple networks/clients
- you see elevated failure rates across multiple models/regions

Macro K-2: “429 quota / rate-limit headers confusion”
A 429 can occur due to either rate limiting (short-term burst control) or quota limits (longer-term account limits). Some clients also misinterpret headers after upgrades.

To narrow this down, can you share:
- 2–3 request IDs returning 429
- response headers (redact auth) for those requests
- your SDK + version

In the meantime:
- Verify you are not retrying aggressively on 429 (use backoff)
- Confirm concurrent request limits in your client (especially after SDK changes)

Macro K-3: “Dedicated autoscaling oscillation (latency spikes)”
If you’re on Dedicated, latency spikes can occur when replicas scale up/down too aggressively for bursty traffic.

Quick checks:
- Does p95 latency spike correlate with scale events?
- Is traffic bursty (high variance) vs steady?

Mitigation options (if you control autoscaling settings):
- Increase minimum replicas
- Increase scale-down cooldown
- Avoid rapid scale-down during peak windows

If you send your Dedicated deployment name, region, and a timestamp window, we can validate scaling behavior and propose a stable configuration.

Macro K-4: “Private installer upgrade stuck / migrations”
For Private upgrades stuck on migrations, the safest next step is to collect installer + cluster diagnostics before further retries.

Please share (redacting secrets):
- installer logs covering the failure
- time window (UTC)
- version you’re upgrading from/to
- any recent cluster changes

If production is impacted, tell us whether rollback is acceptable and what downtime window you have.

Macro K-5: “Audit log delivery latency”
Audit log delivery can be delayed during downstream backlog conditions. To confirm expected vs unexpected behavior, please share:
- region
- time window (UTC)
- approximate volume of audit events
- whether this is continuous or intermittent

Temporary mitigation (if acceptable):
- Increase the lookback window on your export/polling job
- Add retry/backoff on the consumer side

If you need this for compliance deadlines, please flag that explicitly and we’ll prioritize accordingly.

------------------------------------------------------------
E) Comms + expectations (credits / escalation / status)

Macro C-1: “Credits request intake (don’t commit)”
Thanks — we understand the impact and we’re reviewing the timeline against the applicable SLA for your tier.

To proceed, can you confirm:
- impacted time window (UTC)
- affected region/model/endpoint
- approximate request volume affected

We’ll share next steps once we’ve completed the internal review. (We can’t commit to credits until that review is complete.)

Macro C-2: “Status page vs direct customer updates (guidance)”
We’ll continue direct updates in this thread. If this qualifies for a broader service event, we’ll also post a status update.

Note: status updates are reserved for incidents with broader customer impact; not every account-specific issue will appear there.

------------------------------------------------------------
F) Resolution + follow-up

Macro R-1: “Issue resolved + confirm”
Hi {customer_name} — we believe this is resolved as of {resolution_time_utc}.

Summary:
- What happened: {short_summary}
- Mitigation applied: {mitigation}

Can you confirm you’re no longer seeing the issue? If you still see failures, please send 2–3 new request IDs and timestamps.

Macro R-2: “Workaround shared + next step to permanent fix”
We’ve documented the workaround steps here: {kb_link}

This is a mitigation, not a permanent fix. We’re tracking the underlying fix internally and will follow up when it’s deployed broadly.

------------------------------------------------------------
G) Internal notes (library maintenance)

Macro M-1: “Add/update macro checklist”
- Does it ask for request IDs, region, model, time window (UTC)?
- Does it avoid asking for full prompts/responses?
- Does it link to a known-issues article when applicable?
- Does it include clear ‘when to escalate’ guidance?
- Is the update cadence language consistent with tier SLA policy?

Macro M-2: “Sensitive info guardrails (do not include)”
- Internal dashboards links (unless Support-safe + approved)
- PagerDuty schedule names/handles in customer emails
- Internal incident/Sev numbers in customer-facing text
- Capacity details (GPU counts, headroom)
- Any other customer’s data or symptoms

Open questions / TODOs
- Confirm final wording for enterprise update cadence (30 min vs 60 min) per SLA policy sign-off. Owner: Rachel Kim. Due: 2026-02-19.
- Validate which dashboards are “Support-safe quick view” and can be referenced internally in macros. Owner: Allison Grant / Dylan Brooks. (Related: ENG-4823)
- Ensure Jira automation (INT-333) enforces required fields before triage completion: region, model, request IDs/time window.

Change log
- 2026-02-06: Initial draft from known-issues sprint working session (Priya Shah).
- 2026-02-12: Added escalation ask template + waiting-on-customer wording; aligned with Support/SRE playbook notes (Dev Patel, Sean Gallagher).
- 2026-02-18: Added Dedicated autoscaling + Private upgrade + audit log macros; cleaned placeholders; added guardrails section (Owen Phillips, Rachel Kim).
